item.title: NEW: Operation KillSwitch Dismantles KillSec Ransomware Infrastructure
item.description:
Headline: Operation KillSwitch Dismantles KillSec Ransomware Infrastructure

Summary:
A coordinated international law enforcement action, 'Operation KillSwitch,' has successfully dismantled the KillSec ransomware group. The operation led to the arrest of a suspected 16-year-old leader, the seizure of the group's dark web leak site and servers, and the recovery of 110 terabytes of stolen data from nearly 1,000 victims worldwide. The takedown involved agencies from ten countries, with support from Europol and private security firms.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Threat Actor, Incident Response

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: International law enforcement's 'Operation KillSwitch' has dismantled the KillSec ransomware group, leading to arrests and the seizure of its infrastructure and 110TB of stolen data.

Headline: Critical FortiMail Zero-Day (CVE-2026-104286) Actively Exploited

Summary:
Fortinet has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-104286, in its FortiMail secure email gateway. The flaw, rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale, is being actively exploited in the wild. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files, leading to code execution. CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog, mandating urgent mitigation for federal agencies while patches are pending.

item.title: UPDATE: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack
item.description:
Headline: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack

Summary:
Citrix has released emergency patches for eight vulnerabilities in its NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, with two critical zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, confirmed to be under active global exploitation. The flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution, leading to potential webshell deployment and full network compromise. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added both vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating immediate patching and compromise investigation for federal agencies. The attacks were reportedly underway for weeks prior to disclosure, with attackers gaining persistent access to internal networks. Organizations are urged to apply updates immediately and hunt for indicators of compromise, as patching alone does not remediate existing intrusions.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Patch Management

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: Citrix releases urgent patches for two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in NetScaler ADC and Gateway under active exploitation.

The U.S. Department of Defense disclosed a significant data breach from October 2025 that affected the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) through a third-party provider, compromising sensitive personnel data. Separately, secure file transfer company Kiteworks took the drastic step of advising a customer-wide shutdown on September 25 based on 'credible, imminent' federal threat intelligence.
